'''Pascale Senellart''' (born August 21, 1972) is a French physicist who is a senior researcher at the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] and professor at the [[École Polytechnique]]. She has worked on quantum light sources and semiconductor physics. She was awarded the CNRS Silver Medal in 2014, made Fellow of [[The Optical Society]] in 2018, and elected member of the French Academy of Sciences in 2022.

== Early life and education ==
Senellart was born in [[Corbeil-Essonnes]]. She attended the [[École Polytechnique]] as an undergraduate student. She moved to the [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]] for her graduate studies, where she studied non-linear emission from semiconductor microcavities.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Etude de l'émission non-linéaire de microcavités à base de semi-conducteurs III-V en régime de couplage fort|publisher=[s. n.]|date=2001|place=S. l.|language=French|first=Pascale|last=Senellart|oclc=491478949}}</ref> In 2001, Senellart joined the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]] (CNRS).<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-02-04 |title=Pascale Senellart |url=http://www.universite-paris-saclay.fr/en/pascale-senellart |access-date=2024-03-07 |website=Université Paris-Saclay |language=en}}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Senellart has been at the French National Centre for Scientific Research since 2001. When she joined the CNRS she started working in quantum electrodynamics, with a particular focus on semiconductor quantum dots. She developed a novel methodology to control the coupling between a quantum dot and a microcavity.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Prof. Pascale Senellart – Solid-State Quantum Optics|url=http://quantumdot.eu/portfolio/prof-pascale-senellart/|access-date=2021-06-26|language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=The path to perfection: Quantum dots in electrically-controlled cavities yield bright, nearly identical photons|url=https://phys.org/news/2016-06-path-quantum-dots-electrically-controlled-cavities.html|access-date=2021-06-26|website=phys.org|language=en}}</ref> In 2011, she was made a senior researcher and awarded an [[ERC Starting Grant]].<ref name=":0" /> Based on her microcavity designs, Senellart founded the spin-off company [[:fr:Quandela|Quandela]], which develops single photon light sources.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Pascale Senellart|url=https://evenements.bpifrance.fr/qcb-quantum-computing-business/attendee/433d35c1-88f9-ea11-96f5-0003ff29803d|access-date=2021-06-26|website=evenements.bpifrance.fr|language=en}}</ref>
